root_cause.text: In KVM arm64's vgic ITS translation cache invalidation, `vgic_its_invalidate_cache()` used the `xa_for_each()` iterator pointer instead of the value actually returned by atomic `xa_erase()`, so concurrent cache drains from non-mutually-exclusive contexts could drop the same cache-held `vgic_irq` reference multiple times.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that invalidation runs under different locks or no lock at all, allowing concurrent drains, and that the old code did `xa_erase(&its->translation_cache, idx); vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq);` while the fix changes it to `irq = xa_erase(...); if (irq) vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq);`, explicitly ensuring only the context that erased the entry releases the reference.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states that invalidation runs under different locks or no lock at all, allowing concurrent drains, and that the old code did `xa_erase(&its->translation_cache, idx); vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq);` while the fix changes it to `irq = xa_erase(...); if (irq) vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq);`, explicitly ensuring only the context that erased the entry releases the reference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use xa_erase()'s returned entry and only drop the IRQ reference when this context actually removed a cache entry.
intent_record.what: In vgic_its_invalidate_cache(), the code changes from unconditionally calling xa_erase(&its->translation_cache, idx) and then vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq) on the loop variable, to assigning the return value of xa_erase(&its->translation_cache, idx) back to irq, adding a comment that only the erasing context drops the cache reference, and conditionally calling vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq) only if the erased entry returned a non-NULL irq.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the reference release correspond to the object actually removed from the xarray entry and avoids dropping a reference when no entry was erased or when another context already removed it. This prevents incorrect or duplicate vgic_put_irq() calls that could lead to refcount imbalance or use-after-free behavior during cache invalidation.

grouping_result.intent: Use xa_erase()'s returned entry and only drop the IRQ reference when this context actually removed a cache entry.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it switches to using the entry returned by xa_erase() and only releases the vgic_irq reference when this context actually erased the cache entry, preventing duplicate reference drops during concurrent cache invalidation.

candidates.rationale: This drops the reference using the iterator variable instead of the entry actually returned by xa_erase(). If another concurrent invalidation already removed the entry, this context can still call vgic_put_irq() on the same cached vgic_irq, causing a duplicate reference drop.

The return value of xa_erase() was ignored. The root cause is that the code did not use the atomically erased entry to determine whether this context actually removed an item, enabling incorrect reference handling under concurrent cache drains.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement drops the vgic_irq reference using the xa_for_each() iterator variable instead of the entry actually returned by the atomic xa_erase(). Under concurrent cache invalidation, another context may already have erased the entry, yet this code still decrements the same cached IRQ reference, causing a double put.

This statement is vulnerable because it ignores xa_erase()'s return value, which is the only reliable indication of whether this context actually removed a cache entry. Without using that returned entry, the subsequent reference drop can act on an IRQ already removed by another concurrent invalidation.

Author: Oliver Upton <oupton@kernel.org>
Date:   Mon Apr 22 20:01:47 2024 +0000

    KVM: arm64: vgic-its: Maintain a translation cache per ITS
    
    Within the context of a single ITS, it is possible to use an xarray to
    cache the device ID & event ID translation to a particular irq
    descriptor. Take advantage of this to build a translation cache capable
    of fitting all valid translations for a given ITS.
    
    Signed-off-by: Oliver
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the full relevant logic for the per-ITS translation cache and its invalidation, so it is sufficient to judge. The vulnerable construct is present in `vgic_its_invalidate_cache()`: `xa_for_each(&its->translation_cache, idx, irq) { xa_erase(&its->translation_cache, idx); vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq); }`. The root cause described is that invalidation must use the value returned by atomic `xa_erase()` rather than the iterator variable from `xa_for_each()`, because concurrent drains can erase the same entry and the iterator value may no longer correspond to the object actually removed. In this commit, `xa_erase()` is called but its return value is ignored, and `vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq);` uses the iterator pointer `irq` directly. That matches the vulnerable pattern exactly. There is no corrective handling such as `irq = xa_erase(...)` followed by a NULL check before `vgic_put_irq()`, so the fix is not present.
